en: How does a dishwasher use energy and water?
Comparing programmes, calculating cost and water savings
Lifecycle analysis, water-energy nexus and policy
Students will understand how a dishwasher uses energy and water, identify different programme types, and compare hand-washing with machine-washing.
Students will calculate energy and water consumption per cycle, compare programme efficiencies, and evaluate cost savings.
Students will model annual consumption profiles, analyse the water-energy nexus, compare national impacts, and develop evidence-based recommendations.
Dishwasher programme data table (in this worksheet); access to a dishwasher at home or school.
Spreadsheet software; EU energy label data; CO₂ emission factors.

A dishwasher cleans dishes using hot water sprayed at high pressure. It uses electricity mainly to heat the water, and also to pump water and dry the dishes. Understanding how different programmes work helps us choose the most efficient option for each load.
A modern dishwasher uses most of its energy to HEAT WATER. The heating element typically draws 1,500–2,000 W. The pump motor uses only about 50–100 W.
Different programmes heat water to different temperatures:
Eco programme (50 °C): Uses less energy and water, but takes longer (3–4 hours). Most efficient overall.
Normal programme (60 °C): Standard cycle, about 2 hours.
Intensive programme (70 °C): For heavily soiled pots and pans. Uses the most energy and water.
Quick programme (45–60 °C): Shorter cycle, but may use more water per dish because it cleans less thoroughly.
A full dishwasher load typically uses LESS water than washing the same dishes by hand. Hand-washing uses 40–60 litres of water; a modern dishwasher eco cycle uses only 10–12 litres.
**A dishwasher eco programme uses 0.85 kWh and 11 litres of water per cycle.**
**Hand-washing the same dishes uses approximately 50 litres of hot water.**
**The dishwasher uses 0.85 kWh – about 63% less energy than hand-washing!**

Comparing programmes: cost and water savings

At this level you will calculate the exact cost of each dishwasher programme, compare water and energy consumption over a week and a year, and evaluate the financial and environmental benefits of choosing the right programme.

**What you should already know: You should understand how a dishwasher uses energy and water, recognise different programme types (eco, normal, intensive, quick), and know that the eco programme is generally the most efficient.**
The total cost of running a dishwasher depends on both electricity and water:
Total cost per cycle = (Energy × Electricity tariff) + (Water × Water tariff)
The total of electricity cost plus water cost per cycle.
The price per litre of water, including supply and wastewater treatment.

A family runs the dishwasher 5 times per week using the normal programme. Calculate the annual water consumption in litres. Compare this with hand-washing the same number of loads at 50 litres per load.
If the family switches to eco for 4 out of 5 weekly loads (using normal for heavily soiled loads), what is the new annual water consumption? How many litres are saved?

At the advanced level, you will analyse the full environmental impact of dishwasher use, including the water-energy nexus (the energy needed to treat and deliver water), compare national impacts, and develop policy recommendations for reducing dishwasher-related resource consumption.

**What you should already know: You should be able to calculate per-cycle and annual costs for different programmes, compare water and energy consumption, and understand the economic benefits of programme selection.**

THE WATER-ENERGY NEXUS: Water treatment and delivery also consume energy. Treating and delivering 1,000 litres of tap water requires approximately 0.5 kWh. Treating 1,000 litres of wastewater requires an additional 0.7 kWh. So the true energy cost of water use includes this hidden energy.

EU REGULATIONS: Since 2019, dishwashers sold in the EU must not exceed certain energy and water limits. The current regulations push manufacturers toward longer, cooler eco cycles that are more efficient overall despite taking more time.

Approximately 60% of Turkish households (15 million) have a dishwasher. If every household switched from "all normal" to "all eco" programme, calculate the national annual savings in energy (GWh), water (million litres), cost (million €), and CO₂ (thousand tonnes).

Write a 100–150 word policy recommendation for reducing dishwasher energy and water consumption at the national level. Consider: public awareness campaigns, mandatory eco-default settings, EU energy label improvements, and financial incentives. Support your argument with data from your calculations.
